config.title: BER Flight Delay Compensation - FAQ
config.subtitle: When a delayed or cancelled flight from Berlin pays out, how much your route is actually worth, what the airline owes you while you wait, and how to claim it from Germany without paying an agency.

items.q: How late does a flight from BER have to be before I get compensation?
items.a: **Three hours or more, measured at your destination, not in Berlin.** The clock stops when a door of the aircraft is opened at the arrival airport. A flight that leaves BER four hours late but makes up time in the air and lands under three hours behind schedule pays nothing. On a connecting booking it is the arrival at the last airport that counts.

items.q: How much is a delayed flight from Berlin worth?
items.a: **250 euro up to 1,500 kilometres, 400 euro above that, and 600 euro only for long flights outside the EU.** Measured across the 157 destinations BER serves, 79 sit in the 250 euro band, 69 in the 400 euro band and just 9 reach 600 euro. The distance used is the great circle distance from Berlin to your final destination.

items.q: Why is a Tenerife flight only worth 400 euro when it is nearly 3,700 kilometres?
items.a: Because it is an intra-EU flight. The regulation puts **all intra-EU flights over 1,500 kilometres into the 400 euro band regardless of length**, and reserves 600 euro for longer flights that leave the union. Tenerife South is 3,669 kilometres from Berlin and still pays 400 euro. Gran Canaria, Fuerteventura, Lanzarote and Funchal work the same way. Dubai, at 4,613 kilometres, pays 600 euro.

items.q: What is the airline required to give me while I wait at BER?
items.a: **Meals and refreshments in proportion to the wait, plus two calls or emails, and a hotel with transfer if the new departure is the next day.** The trigger is two hours for flights up to 1,500 kilometres, three hours for intra-EU flights over 1,500 kilometres and other flights up to 3,500, and four hours beyond that. This right to care applies even when weather or air traffic control means no compensation is due. Past five hours you can abandon the trip and claim a refund.

items.q: When can the airline legally refuse to pay?
items.a: **Extraordinary circumstances**, meaning weather, air traffic control decisions, political instability and security risks. Most technical faults do not count, because maintaining an aircraft is the airline's ordinary business, and a strike by the airline's own staff does not count either. A cancellation announced more than 14 days ahead pays nothing. Giving up your seat voluntarily on an overbooked flight also ends the claim.

items.q: Did the EU change the rules in 2026?
items.a: The revision was approved by the European Parliament on **7 July 2026 by 646 votes to 12** and cleared by the Council on 13 July 2026, but it enters into force twenty days after publication and then allows a further year, so it applies from **2027**. The three hour threshold and the 250, 400 and 600 euro amounts survived the rewrite unchanged. Until then a delay out of BER is judged under the rules in force since 2004.

items.q: How do I claim, and how long do I have?
items.a: Write to the airline first with the flight number, date, booking reference, scheduled arrival and actual arrival, name Regulation 261/2004 and ask for a **bank transfer rather than a voucher**. If it refuses or ignores you, the free arbitration body Schlichtungsstelle Reise & Verkehr, formerly söp, is based in Berlin and costs the passenger nothing. The Luftfahrt-Bundesamt supervises airlines but will not collect the money for you. In Germany the claim expires **three years after the end of the calendar year of the flight**.

items.q: Should I leave the airport if my flight from BER is badly delayed?
items.a: If the new departure is **at least four hours away and you have not dropped a bag**, yes. The station is directly under Terminal 1, the Airport Express reaches Berlin Hauptbahnhof in 22 minutes and Alexanderplatz in about 32 minutes with one change, and an ABC ticket costs 5.00 euro single or 12.90 euro for 24 hours. If you are already through security, stay put: the queue is unpredictable and you would be starting again.
